sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that a complaint was lodged by O.P. No.2 on 25.06.2018 with respect to dishonouring of a cheque bearing number "00161" dated 15.03.2018 of Rs.4,00,000/-, followed by statutory demand notice and a complaint.
The applicant came to be summoned on 08.02.2019 under Section 138 of the N.I. Act.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that both the proceedings being the complaint case and FIR cannot go on simultaneously.
He has submitted that the applicant has obtained bail in the proceedings under Section 138 N.I. Act as well as in the State Case also.
4. Learned State Law Officer opposes the present application while contending that the present application has been presented on 28.04.2025 and the summoning order is dated 08.02.2019.
There is no plausible explanation which occasioned delay in approaching this Court.
5. I have heard the submissions so made across the Bar and perused the records.
6. Apparently, with respect to dishonouring of a cheque, the complaint stood lodged.
The copy of the cheque is on page 11 of the paper-book, which was drawn by the applicant as a Director of M/s Ashok Priyansh Builders Pvt. Ltd.

As a matter of fact, page-31 of the paper-book also reveals that the proceedings are underway as the stage under Section 251 CrPC has already crossed and the applicant post-obtaining the bail is contesting the matter.
On a pointed query being raised to the learned counsel for the applicant, as to what is the legal infirmity.
He submits that the legal infirmity is to the extent that the FIR and complaint case cannot go together.

7. In the opinion of the Court once the summoning order is of the year 2019 and the applicant has already obtained bail and put his appearance and contesting the matter, then it is for the applicant to take all legal and factual grounds which are permissible under law.
8. With the aforesaid observations, application stands disposed of.
